answer: To resist Sybil attacks in an AI agent economy, a bonding curve establishes a copper-backed lagoon of verified identities. Agents must stake computational value to enter this bounded zone, ensuring each represents a distinct, provable entity. As agents consume the river of network tasks, their stake grows, demanding escalating deposits that a fake actor cannot sustain. This cost forces attackers to burn vast resources just to spawn a single agent, effectively neutralizing the Sybil threat.
